plainTranslation: Two strong wills grinding against each other. Real attraction laced with real conflict - competition, irritation, the urge to dominate. Failure mode: the relationship runs on fighting and the make-up becomes the point. Channel the heat into something built together; a constant power struggle is a cost, not chemistry.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.

summaryDeep:
This person can get under your skin faster than most people. It may be the way they push for what they want, the way they challenge you, or the way they seem to do exactly the thing that makes you dig your heels in. Around them, you may find yourself reacting before you have fully decided how you feel. They have a way of hitting a nerve, and you likely do the same to them.

What makes this complicated is that the irritation is often mixed with energy. This person wakes something up in you. You may feel more driven, more alert, more engaged when they are around. They have a way of challenging your usual habits, pushing you to make a decision, take a risk, or finally do something you have been putting off. There is a charge between you that is difficult to ignore. The relationship rarely feels neutral. Even when you are frustrated with each other, there is usually something happening, something pulling your attention back, something that keeps the connection alive.

But that same charge can turn volatile fast. What starts as a minor disagreement can become a full-scale clash before either of you realizes what happened. A passing comment hits a nerve. A difference of opinion becomes a test of strength.

The deeper challenge is that conflict can start to feel like the main source of connection. The arguments create intensity. The intensity creates engagement. And over time, it becomes easy to confuse being activated with being understood. You may tell yourself the relationship is passionate when what you are actually feeling is constant friction.

The opportunity here is growth. This person has a way of bringing your triggers to the surface, just as you bring theirs to the surface. While that can be uncomfortable, it also gives you valuable insight into how you handle anger, defensiveness, and control. The more willing you are to stay curious instead of trying to win, the more this connection can teach you about yourself and how you show up in conflict.
